ko.executive_summary: Qualcomm announces broad Snapdragon chip price increases effective September 1 amid component shortages, which will drive up Android smartphone costs. Smartphone SoC shipments are declining as memory prices surge, though AI chips show strong 24% growth, pushing Samsung's Exynos into greater strategic importance.

implications.text: Qualcomm's September price increase will compress Android OEM margins and likely result in higher retail device prices
SoC pricing dynamics elevate Exynos as alternative to Snapdragon for price-sensitive segments
24% AI chip growth contrasts with SoC weakness, signaling market shift toward AI-capable processors

ko.counterpoint: Component shortage justification for price hikes may face pushback from OEMs and carriers given mixed market conditions.

ko.executive_summary: SK hynix is comprehensively overhauling its recruitment system to prioritize AI-era talent acquisition, eliminating educational credentials and implementing half-day deep interviews and AI capability assessments. This marks a critical talent strategy shift in response to semiconductor industry boom and heightened competition for AI expertise.
key_facts: SK hynix launches massive August recruitment push
AI capability assessment added to screening

implications.text: SK hynix restructuring mirrors broader semiconductor industry race to secure AI-capable engineering talent amid explosive demand
Removal of credential barriers signals industry recognition that traditional educational gatekeeping poorly predicts AI-era skill requirements
Alignment with Samsung's open recruitment strategy indicates elevated stakes in HPC/datacenter talent competition

ko.counterpoint: Large-scale hiring during potential market cyclicality poses execution risk if AI demand softens.

ko.executive_summary: Amazon and Google are scaling custom silicon production to challenge Nvidia, with Amazon's chip business reaching $25B and Google targeting 15 million AI chips by 2028. MediaTek is also expanding AI accelerators with Q4 mass production plans and raising data center revenue targets above $2 billion while pushing ASIC market share to 15-20%.
key_facts: Google target: 15 million AI chips by 2028
MediaTek Q4 AI accelerator mass production
MediaTek data center revenue target: >$2 billion
Ericsson custom silicon deployed across all three Japan carriers
Flip chip technology market growing from $37.98B (2025) to $73.46B (2035)

implications.text: Amazon and Google custom silicon reaching scale threatens Nvidia's monopoly; combined with MediaTek expansion, hyperscaler/fabless diversification accelerating
MediaTek and Ericsson moves signal ASIC and custom silicon becoming table-stakes for telecom and enterprise segments
Intel seizing opportunity as TSMC faces AI chip packaging constraints; advanced packaging technology (flip chip) doubling market size over decade

ko.counterpoint: Custom silicon requires sustained investment and long design cycles; hyperscaler execution risk remains if in-house programs face delays or cost overruns.

ko.executive_summary: Samsung targets Taylor Fab 2 groundbreaking by end-2026 with 2030 mass production and 1.4nm expansion plans, while TSMC pulls forward 1.4nm to H1 2028 ahead of Samsung and Intel competition. Omdia raises 2026 revenue forecast 94.1% on AI-driven demand, and SK Siltronic wafer supplier is acquired by Doosan for approximately 2.3 trillion won, while ASE raises CapEx to record $10.5B.
key_facts: Samsung Taylor Fab 2 groundbreaking: end-2026 target, 2030 mass production
SK Siltronic acquisition: ~2.3 trillion won by Doosan
SK Siltronic founded 1983, specializes in semiconductor wafers
ASE advanced packaging revenue goal: 2x by 2027

implications.text: TSMC's acceleration to H1 2028 for 1.4nm underscores competitive urgency; Samsung's end-2026 groundbreaking signals sustained foundry capacity buildup
94.1% AI-driven revenue growth forecast justifies record CapEx; ASE and foundries racing to scale advanced packaging as bottleneck
SK Siltronic sale to Doosan reflects SK's strategic exit from wafer manufacturing to focus on memory; removes mid-tier Korean competitor

ko.counterpoint: Massive CapEx commitments assume sustained AI demand; cyclical downturn could strand fabs with underutilized capacity.
